# Error codes

Status: v1 reference client — pre-release; no sandbox server is bundled in this
repository. The codes below are the planned wire contract: the server table is
the stable shared vocabulary, the condition table binds contract-level
rejections, and the client table lists codes the reference client raises
locally when no server error object applies.

## Stable wire codes (server)

These wire strings are part of the cross-language contract and must not drift.

| Rust variant (`NativeErrorCode`) | Wire code | HTTP status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InvalidArgument` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | 400 | The request violates the v1 contract (bad identifier, missing or duplicate command form, non-positive resource value, oversize input). Fix the request; replaying it verbatim will fail again. |
| `NotFound` | `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The addressed resource does not exist. A stale generation on an otherwise valid id is also a lookup failure, not a success. |
| `Conflict` | `CONFLICT` | 409 | The request conflicts with current resource state (for example a generation mismatch or an illegal lifecycle transition). Re-read state before retrying. |
| `PreconditionFailed` | `PRECONDITION_FAILED` | 412 | A host capability or policy precondition is unmet; the request is rejected before any resource is created. Nothing is silently downgraded. |
| `Unavailable` | `UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | The addressed backend or capability is unavailable on this host right now. |
| `Internal` | `INTERNAL` | 500 | An internal server fault. Report it with the returned request id. |

## Contract-level condition codes (`contracts/v1/resolution-rules.json`)

Requirement/policy rejections carry their own condition codes on top of the
HTTP status:

| Code | HTTP status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `HOST_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` | 412 | A `true` requirement whose mapped host capability is not SUPPORTED; rejected before create with no fallback rewriting. |
| `POLICY_UNSUPPORTED` | 412 | The single-ID compatibility policy (STRICT by default) refuses unfaithful UID/GID expressions at create/preflight. |

## Reference-client codes

Raised by the client itself (or defaulted when a response lacks a structured
code). They never indicate success and are never retried implicitly.

| Code | Raised as / by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `HTTP_ERROR` | `ApiError` (client fallback) | HTTP failure without a structured error code in the response body. |
| `OPERATION_AMBIGUOUS` | `OperationUnknown` (client) | The operation reported status `unknown`; it requires server-side reconciliation before its outcome can be trusted. |
| `OPERATION_FAILED` | `ApiError` (operation) | The operation reached status `failed`. This is the default code when the server error object carries a message but no code. |
| `PROTOCOL_ERROR` | `ApiError` (client) | The response was not the expected JSON object, or an operation error had an unexpected shape. |
| `REQUEST_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | `AmbiguousRequest` (client) | A non-GET response was lost in transit. The original request must be queried by idempotency key before any resubmission — the client never retries implicitly. |
| `TRANSPORT_ERROR` | `ApiError` (client) | A GET/HEAD request could not reach the API transport. Non-GET requests never surface this — a lost response is REQUEST_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN instead. |
| `WAIT_TIMEOUT` | `WaitTimeout` (client) | The client wait deadline elapsed while polling an operation. The server-side operation was NOT cancelled by the timeout. |

## CLI exit codes

The `lsbx` CLI maps the above onto process exit codes for scripting:

| Exit | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success, including dry-run previews (`"executed": false`). |
| 2 | Usage or client-side contract error (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`). |
| 8 | `WAIT_TIMEOUT` — the wait deadline elapsed; the operation still exists server-side. |
| 10 | `REQUEST_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` or `OPERATION_AMBIGUOUS` — outcome must be reconciled before resubmission. |
| 11 | Any other API error (including `INVALID_ARGUMENT` returned by a server). |
